title: Generation and Quantitative Characterization of Functional and Polarized Biliary Epithelial Cysts
protocol: Thaw the hydrogel at 4°C overnight.
Precool pipette tips on ice or overnight at -20°C.
Precool an 8-well chamber slide overnight at -20°C.
Place the hydrogel and the 8-well chamber slide in an ice bucket filled with ice.
Prepare a solution containing 40% hydrogel in cold NRC complete medium and place it on ice.
Using cold pipette tips, add 50 μL of hydrogel solution to the center of each well on the chamber slide.
Spread the hydrogel solution evenly over the entire surface of each well using a pipette tip while holding the chamber slide on ice.
Incubate the chamber slide for at least 15 minutes at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Warm up NRC complete medium in a water bath preheated to 37°C.
Warm up phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) in a water bath preheated to 37°C.
Warm up trypsin-ethylenediamine tetraacetic acid (trypsin-EDTA) in a water bath preheated to 37°C.
Wash NRCs once with pre-heated 1x PBS.
Incubate NRCs with 5 mL of pre-heated 1x PBS for 20 min at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Discard the PBS and add 1 mL of trypsin-EDTA.
Incubate the cells with trypsin-EDTA for 5-10 min at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Neutralize the solution with 4 mL of pre-heated complete NRC medium.
Collect and transfer the cell suspension into a 15 mL conical tube.
Spin the cell suspension at 150 x g for 4 min.
Discard the medium and resuspend the cell pellet in 5 mL of pre-heated medium.
Filter the cell solution through a 40 μm cell strainer into a 50 mL conical tube.
Count the cells.
Prepare a solution of 1,600 µL of 80% hydrogel (V/V) in cold complete NRC medium and keep it on ice.
Dilute 5 x 10^5 cells/mL in 1,600 µL of cold complete NRC medium and keep it on ice.
Mix tube 1 and tube 2 to prepare a cell seeding solution of 2.5 x 10^5 cells/mL in 40% hydrogel.
Add 400 μL of the cell solution into each well of the hydrogel-coated chamber slide, avoiding bubbles.
Keep the chamber slide in an incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2 until media change.
Remove 250 μL of medium from a corner of each well after 2 days in culture, being careful not to pipette out the hydrogel.
Slowly add 250 μL of fresh culture medium.
Change the medium every 2 days.
Take a Z-stack along the depth of the hydrogel for each time point using phase-contrast microscopy and serial imaging (Z-stacks).
Select the 10x objective magnification in the manual nose-piece pad window with an image acquisition software.
Switch on the white lamp and select the brightfield imaging option.
Switch the camera on by selecting the “Play” button in the bar submenu.
Focus on a field of cysts and set the exposure time.
Open the Auto Capture Folder window for automatic saving of images.
Open the capture Z-series window and define with the Z screw the top and bottom planes of the Z-stack.
Adjust the Z-step depending on the objective, the level of resolution, and press the button “Run now” to launch the acquisition.
Take at least 3 non-overlapping Z-stacks per well.
Open the Fiji software.
Open the Z-stack using File | Open from the Fiji menu.
Select “Virtual Stack” option if needed and click “Yes” for opening.
Duplicate the stack via Image | Duplicate.
Create a minimum intensity projection from the duplicated stack.
Go to the Image menu | Stacks | Z Project.
Select Projection type “Min Intensity” and click “OK”.
Subtract the background from the projection.
Go to the Process menu | Subtract Background.
Type 500.0 pixels of rolling ball radius.
Click “light background” to render cysts more contrasted than the background.
If contrast enhancement is needed, go to Image menu | Adjust | Brightness/Contrast | Auto | Apply.
Set the lower and upper gray values as required for optimal visualization.
If the projection is not calibrated, go to Analyze menu | Set scale.
Type the corresponding calibration µm/pixel ratio.
Select the Straight-line tool in the Fiji menu.
Draw a line across the diameter of each cyst on the final projection.
Add the new region of interest (ROI) created for each cyst to the ROI manager.
Press the “t” shortcut on the keyboard for faster counting and opening of the ROI manager.
Click “Show All” to see the counted cysts.
Check that no cyst has been left without counting by superimposing the set ROIs from the projection on the Z-stack.
In the ROI Manager, click “Show All.”
Move the cursor along the Z-stack to check that image per image, all cysts have been counted.
Select the ROI set and save it via the ROI Manager window by clicking More | Save.
Select all ROIs in the ROI Manager and click “Measure” in the ROI Manager to get the size of each cyst.
Open a new window of measurements named “Results.”
Number each cyst and its estimated size.
Save the results in .csv format by clicking on the “Results” window and via the menu: File | Save As.
Prepare a stock solution of fluorescein diacetate (FDA) by dissolving 5 mg in 1 mL acetone and store at -20°C.
Prepare a stock solution of propidium iodide (PI) at a concentration of 2 mg/mL in deionized water and store at 4°C.
Prepare NRC medium without fetal calf serum (FCS).
Add 4 μL of FDA stock solution and 25 μL of PI stock solution into 2.5 mL of NRC medium without FCS to prepare the staining solution.
Remove the medium from the chamber slide.
Add 250 μL of staining solution into each well and incubate for 4-5 minutes in the dark at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Pipette out the staining solution carefully.
Wash once with 250 μL of 1x PBS.
Carefully add 250 μL of complete NRC medium to each well.
Take pictures using an inverted fluorescence microscope with Texas red and FITC filters.
Add 0.83 μL of Hoechst stock solution (15 mg/mL) in 2.5 mL of NRC medium without FCS to prepare a staining solution at 5 μg/mL.
Incubate the Hoechst solution with cells for 15 min at 37 °C, 5% CO₂.
Remove the Hoechst solution and add 250 µL of FDA solution (8 μg/mL final concentration) to each well.
Incubate the wells with FDA solution for 4-5 minutes at 37 °C, 5% CO₂.
Take pictures every minute for 1 hour via time-lapse imaging.
Take images using an inverted fluorescence microscope 5 min after rinsing with medium without FCS.
Use DAPI and FITC filters to reveal nuclei labeling and fluorescein accumulation in the lumen.
Prepare a stock solution of 10 mM Verapamil in dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO).
Mix 2.5 μL of Verapamil stock solution with 2.5 mL culture medium without FCS to prepare a 10 µM working solution.
Add 250 µL of Verapamil working solution into each well and incubate for 20 min at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Remove the Verapamil solution and add 250 μL of FDA solution (8 μg/mL final concentration) into each well.
Incubate in the dark for 4-5 min at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Wash with 250 µL of 1x PBS before imaging.
Mix 4% formaldehyde with 5% sucrose in 1x PBS, pH 7.4.
Incubate the mixture in a water bath pre-heated to 37 °C.
Gently pipette out the culture medium from the well without damaging the matrix.
Slowly add 400 μL of fixing solution to the side of the wells.
Incubate for 20 min at room temperature (RT).
Leave 25 μL of liquid above the matrix to prevent damage.
Gently remove the fixing solution and wash 3 times with 400 μL of 1x PBS at RT.
Pipette out the PBS, add 400 μL of permeabilization solution (0.5% Triton X-100 in 1x PBS) and incubate for 10 min at RT.
Gently remove the permeabilization solution and wash 3 times quickly with 400 μL of 1x PBS.
Wash once more with 400 μL of PBS/0.05% Tween 20 and discard.
Add 400 μL of blocking solution containing 0.1% bovine serum albumin (BSA) and 10% goat serum in 1x PBS and incubate for 60 min at RT.
Pipette out the blocking solution, wash once with 400 μL of PBS/0.05% Tween 20, and discard.
Add 150 μL of antibody solution, e.g., E-cadherin antibody diluted 1:400 and Phalloidin 568 (16.2 nM final concentration) in 1x PBS, and incubate for 90 min at RT.
Wash the sample with 400 µL of PBS/0.05% Tween 20, three times; each time incubating the sample for 10 min at RT.
Add 150 µL of secondary antibody (goat anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor Plus 647), diluted 1:500 in 1x PBS and incubate 60 min at RT.
Wash the sample with 400 µL of PBS/0.05% Tween 20, three times; each time incubating the sample for 10 min at RT.
Wash the sample with 400 µL of 1x PBS, three times; each time incubating the sample for 10 min at RT.
Discard the PBS from the last wash and prepare the chamber slide for visualization via confocal microscopy following one of the two options below.
Add 400 μL of 1x PBS and 50 µL of DAPI per well, allowing examination through the bottom of the well without a coverslip.
Add 100 µL per well of antifade reagent containing DAPI and let the slide dry overnight at RT.
